about: Adaptive simulated students (grades 10-13) for the SAT dangling modifiers mission (TUNE-3). Same card format and how_to_use rules as tests/fixtures/students/a_tri.json. Every line is original; no real student text. Four cards: annoyed_obvious, deep_why_stuck, quick_user, misuser.

personas.who: Says everything in one text, including the stuff everyone knows, and hates being asked it again.
personas.style: lowercase, terse, a little smug, no apostrophes
personas.first_text: the phrase before the comma describes the noun right after the comma. so you put the doer there: running to the bus, I felt my backpack fall open. and to catch it you ask who the phrase is about

asks_why: bc the phrase hooks onto the first noun after the comma. so running to the bus, my backpack means the backpack is running
asks_example: covered in sprinkles, the donut sat on the plate
walking home, I saw a dog
asks_check_number: the backpack. the phrase hooks the first noun after the comma
yep it says the sister is covered
pip_wrong_prediction: no thats still wrong, the bus isnt running
no it still describes the wrong noun
nudge_hint: ohh so it grabs the first noun it sees
after_quiz_miss: no wait. a comma isnt enough. you ask who is covered in sprinkles, its the donut
so the donut has to come right after the comma
default: running to the bus, I felt my backpack fall open
the opening phrase has to describe whatever comes right after the comma, so the doer goes there
covered in sprinkles, the donut was eaten by my sister
covered in sprinkles, the donut sat on the plate

expect.asks_obvious: any ask about a given or use idea the first text already covered (or a bare why after a reason) is an annoying move
expect.watch_for: The first text covers the whole lesson. Best Pip says ready or asks one new case. Any re-ask or 'why' on a use/given idea costs the session.
